axes.twist: it has to look premium on a tiny budget

prompt: I run a tiny nonprofit called Patch Bay Collective that loans out Eurorack modules and runs free synth workshops for teens and college kids, and I need a donation page built as a single index.html in this folder with all CSS and JS inline, no frameworks, no build step, and no external images (use CSS gradients, SVG drawn inline, or pure type for visuals, maybe a little animated patch cable or oscillator waveform as the hero). We have basically zero design budget but I want it to feel like a boutique synth brand's site, not a church bake sale: think tight typography, dark panel aesthetic with knob/jack details, restrained accent color, generous spacing. The audience is mostly Gen Z so keep the copy casual and honest, no corporate guilt-trip tone, and make it great on phones first. It needs a short mission blurb, preset donation tiers framed like gear ($10 "patch cable", $25 "a VCA", $100 "a full module loaned out for a semester") plus a custom amount, a monthly/one-time toggle, a few quick impact stats, a small FAQ accordion, and a donate button that just shows a thank-you state for now since we haven't hooked up payments yet.
